function: SAC (centralized) and MASAC (distributed) agents learn AP active beamforming and STAR-RIS transmission and reflection amplitudes and phases to maximize long-term sum-rate under user QoS (p. 6-7, p. 9).
system: Downlink cell-free mMIMO: 4 APs with 2 antennas, 4 single-antenna users, 2 energy-splitting STAR-RISs of 16 elements, 1 MHz; carrier frequency not stated (p. 4-5, p. 11).
method: Soft actor-critic: centralized SAC and multi-agent MASAC with centralized training and decentralized execution; DNNs with two hidden layers, Adam; online reinforcement learning (p. 6-9, p. 11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician channels with Rayleigh NLoS and distance path loss, quasi-static block fading, 2-D layout with mobile users; no 3GPP model or measurement (p. 5, p. 11).
test_conditions: Training curves over 2000 episodes of 30 slots (p. 11, p. 13); curves per N in {8,16,24,32} and K in {4,8}, 5% CSI error; no test in unseen setting (p. 13-15).
baselines: Scheme baselines under the same SAC/MASAC: no STAR-RIS, random STAR-RIS phases/amplitudes, single-sided RIS, dual-sided RIS; learned: MADDPG (p. 14), earlier full-load SAC [1] (p. 13).
metrics: Average EWMA episode reward (sum-rate minus QoS penalty), average sum-rate in Mbps, and average number of users meeting the QoS rate (p. 7, p. 12-15).
complexity: Analytical order O(W x weights of critic and actor networks) for SAC and MASAC, with fronthaul data per slot; no runtime or FLOPs (p. 8, p. 10).
q1_support: p. 5: "we employ a Rician fading channel model to represent these channels"; p. 11 uses a custom power-law path loss. No 3GPP model, ray-tracing dataset, or measurement is used, so the channel is a custom simulator.
q2_support: p. 14: "algorithms in 4-user and 8-user scenarios". Each setting (N, K, CSI error) has its own training curve over episodes (Figs. 9-13); the paper never tests a trained agent in a setting not used for training. The 5% CSI error (p. 15) is an error sweep.
q3_support: p. 11: "STAR-RIS elements have random phase shifts and amplitude coefficients" (random RIS, sum-rate in Fig. 7); p. 14: "MASAC-based and SAC-based algorithms consistently achieve significantly higher average EWMA episode rewards than MADDPG" (Fig. 12).
q4_support: p. 8: "computational complexity of the SAC algorithm is O" followed by the weight counts of the critic and actor networks; p. 10 gives the same for the MASAC training and execution phases.
q5_support: p. 11: "we use a 2-D scenario of a multi-STAR-RISs-aided CF mMIMO network"; the channels come from a custom simulator (p. 5) and the paper gives no code or data link.
notes: Title page 1 matches the DOI. Included, area 3: DRL learns the AP precoders and the STAR-RIS coefficients (p. 6-7). q3 judgment for the reviewer: Random-STAR is the non-learned random RIS baseline although its active beamforming is still learned (p. 11); MADDPG is the standard learned baseline compared on reward (p. 14, Fig. 12); the full-load SAC of the authors' conference paper [1] is also compared (p. 13). The footnote on p. 1 prints this paper's own DOI as the conference DOI; ignored. Carrier frequency is never stated. p. 11 states M = 4 APs but lists eight AP locations; the text value M = 4 is used.
